content: The test image shows a corn plant with striking white/yellow parallel striping alternating with green tissue along the entire length of leaves, with some leaves appearing shredded. This pattern strongly suggests Downy mildew or Maize streak virus. Let me compare reference images.

**Candidate comparison:**
- **Maize streak virus**: Reference bottom-right panel shows exactly this — alternating white and green parallel bands running along the leaf, same bold pattern as test image. MSV is endemic to Africa, transmitted by leafhoppers, causes characteristic pale-to-white stripes on leaves.
- **Maize dwarf mosaic virus**: Reference shows similar striping but more yellow/green mosaic; top-right panel shows similar white stripes in African red-soil setting — also a close match.
- **Downy mildew**: Reference images show mostly green plants with no bold striping — eliminated.

The broad, continuous white-to-cream parallel stripes covering the entire leaf length (not broken mosaic flecks) and the African field context point most strongly to **Maize streak virus**.
